newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds tracked bunds to a firmer close as an auction in Germany proceeded smoothly and prices got a boost from speculation that upcoming German unemployment data might turn out higher than expected.
Dealers said a higher jobless total on Thursday might prompt the Bundesbank to cut its repo rate during the first quarter.
The guilder market saw an inflow of funds switched out of non-core European currencies but dealers said funds were also shifted out of guilders and into bunds.
Dealers said the firmer tone may well persist on Wednesday but that the subsequent outlook depended on U.S. producer prices and payrolls data due on Thursday and Friday respectively.
Details of a new Dutch state bond issue, or re-opening of an earlier issue, are due to be announced on Friday January 17.
Some dealers expect this to be a new 2007 maturity, though others tip a reopening of the September 2002 bond.

"I think the state wants to reduce the maturity of its debt. A reopening of the September 2002 bond would make sense because there is only seven billion guilders outstanding at the moment," said one dealer. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
